questions.q: Who was Noah’s ancestor, going back to Adam?
questions.a: Seth, Enosh, Kenan, Mahalalel, Jared, Enoch, Methuselah, and Lamech were Noah’s ancestors, going back to Adam.

questions.q: Who were the sons of Japheth?
questions.a: Japheth’s sons were Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.

questions.q: Who were the sons of Ham?
questions.a: Ham’s sons were Cush, Egypt, Put, and Canaan.

questions.q: Who was the first man to become a mighty warrior on the earth?
questions.a: Nimrod, the son of Cush, was the first man to become a mighty warrior on the earth.

questions.q: Who did Canaan become the ancestor of?
questions.a: Canaan became the ancestor of Sidon, his firstborn, and of the Hittites, Jebusites, Amorites, Girgashites, Hivites, Arkites, Sinites, Arvadites, Zemarites, and Hamathites.

questions.q: Who were the sons of Shem?
questions.a: Shem’s sons were Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, and Aram.

questions.q: Why was one of Eber’s sons named Peleg?
questions.a: During his lifetime, God divided the people of the earth into groups.

questions.q: Who was Terah’s ancestor, going back to Shem?
questions.a: Arpachshad, Shelah, Eber, Peleg, Reu, Serug, and Nahor were Terah’s ancestors, going back to Shem.

questions.q: What was Abram’s name later changed to?
questions.a: Abram’s name was later changed to Abraham.

questions.q: Who were the sons of Abraham?
questions.a: Abraham’s sons were Isaac and Ishmael.

questions.q: Who were the sons of Ishmael?
questions.a: Ishmael’s sons were Nebaioth, his firstborn, Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam, Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.

questions.q: Who were the sons of Keturah, Abraham’s concubine?
questions.a: Keturah’s sons were Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.

questions.q: Who were the sons of Isaac?
questions.a: Isaac’s sons were Esau and Israel.

questions.q: Who were the sons of Esau?
questions.a: Esau’s sons were Eliphaz, Reuel, Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.

questions.q: What land had kings before kings reigned over the Israelites?
questions.a: The land of Edom had kings before the Israelites had kings.

questions.q: Who became king after Husham died, and what did he do?
questions.a: Hadad, the son of Bedad, became king after Husham died. He defeated the Midianites in the country of Moab.

questions.q: Who ruled Edom as chiefs after Hadad died?
questions.a: After Hadad died, Edom was ruled by chiefs named Timna, Alvah, Jetheth, Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon, Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar, Magdiel, and Iram.

commentary.text: Verses 1–27 This chapter, and many that follow, repeat the genealogies, or lists of fathers and children in the Bible history, and put them together, with many added. When compared with other places, there are some differences found; yet we must not therefore stumble at the word, but bless God that the things necessary to salvation are plain enough. The original of the Jewish nation is here traced from the first man that God created, and is thereby distinguished from the obscure, fabulous, and absurd origins assigned to other nations. But the nations now are all so mingled with one another, that no one nation, nor the greatest part of any, is descended entirely from any of one nation, nor the greatest part of any, is descended entirely from any of these fountains. Only this we are sure of, that God has created of one blood all nations of men; they are all descended from one Adam, one Noah. Have we not all one father? Has not one God created us? Mal 2:10.

The genealogy is from hence confined to the posterity of Abraham. Let us take occasion from reading these lists of names, to think of the multitudes that have gone through this world, have done their parts in it, and then quitted it. As one generation, even of sinful men, passes away, another comes. Ec 1:4; Nu 32:14, and will do so while the earth remains. Short is our passage through time into eternity. May we be distinguished as the Lord's people.
